headline: A door plug blows out of a new 737 MAX 9
text: On 5 January a door plug blew out of an Alaska Airlines 737 MAX 9 shortly after take-off from Portland; all 177 people on board survived. The FAA grounded similar planes, and inspections found loose parts on others. Chief executive Dave Calhoun admitted a 'quality escape', and the FAA opened an investigation into Boeing's production.
imageCaption: The Alaska Airlines 737 MAX 9 with the missing door plug area covered, January 2024

headline: Tesla warns growth will slow
text: Tesla said on 24 January that its vehicle volume growth in 2024 'may be notably lower' than in 2023, as it is 'between two major growth waves' and works on a cheaper next-generation car.
source: Tesla Q4 and FY 2023 Update, 24 January 2024, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000095017024007073/tsla-ex99_1.htm (read 2026-10-03); WSJ, 'Tesla Projects Slower Growth in 2024 as EV Demand Softens', 24 January 2024 (headline via Google News) (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: A Tesla Cybertruck, 2024

headline: Nikkei beats its 1989 record, 34 years later
text: On 22 February the Nikkei closed at 39,098.68, above its record of 38,915.87 set on 29 December 1989. Foreign investors are buying Japan as companies reform and prices rise again, and as money leaves China.
imageCaption: The Tokyo Stock Exchange

headline: Prices up 7.5%, volumes down
text: Nestlé reported 2023 organic growth of 7.2% on 22 February, but almost all of it came from higher prices (7.5%); the volume of goods sold fell 0.3%. For 2024 it expects organic growth of about 4%. Chief executive Mark Schneider spoke of unprecedented inflation and soft consumer demand.
imageCaption: Kit Kat, one of Nestlé's best-known products

headline: Two trillion dollars
text: On 1 March Nvidia closed with a stock market value above two trillion dollars, only the third US company to do so, 180 days after passing one trillion. Technology companies are buying tens of thousands of its H100 chips, which sell for 25,000 to 30,000 dollars each.
imageCaption: Endeavor, one of Nvidia's headquarters buildings in Santa Clara, California

headline: GE Vernova spun off: what remains is GE Aerospace
text: On 2 April General Electric completed the spin-off of its energy businesses as GE Vernova. The remaining company, which makes and services jet engines, now trades as GE Aerospace.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GE_Vernova (read 2026-10-03, citing GE Vernova press release 2024-04-02); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Electric (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: A GE Haliade-X offshore wind turbine

headline: Intel's factories lost 7 billion dollars
text: On 2 April Intel published separate figures for its manufacturing business for the first time: Intel Foundry lost 7 billion dollars in 2023 on sales of 18.9 billion, and Gelsinger expects 2024 losses to be the worst, with break-even around 2027. The shares fell 8% the next day. On 25 April a weak forecast for the second quarter followed.
source: https://www.cnbc.com/2024/04/02/intel-shares-fall-after-company-reveals-7-billion-operating-loss-in-foundry-business.html (read 2026-10-03, via search summary); https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/intel-foundry-unit-posts-25bn-operating-loss-for-q1-2024/ (read 2026-10-03, via search summary)
imageCaption: President Obama speaks at Intel's Fab 42, Chandler, Arizona, January 2012

headline: SLB agrees to buy ChampionX
text: On 2 April SLB agreed to buy ChampionX, a maker of production chemicals and artificial-lift pumps that keep old wells flowing, in an all-share deal: 0.735 SLB shares per ChampionX share, about 7.75 billion dollars. ChampionX owners will hold about 9 percent of SLB. SLB also raised its target for returns to shareholders to 3 billion dollars this year and 4 billion in 2025.
source: SLB and ChampionX press release of 2 April 2024, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/87347/000119312524084191/ (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schlumberger (value) (read 2026-10-03); SLB Form 8-K of 16 July 2025 (closing), https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/87347/000119312525159859/ (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Pumpjacks silhouetted at sunset

headline: Nemo wins Eurovision for Switzerland
text: The Swiss singer Nemo won the Eurovision Song Contest in Malmö on 11 May with 'The Code', winning the combined and the jury vote. Nemo is the first openly non-binary winner. Switzerland will host the contest next year.
imageCaption: Nemo with the Eurovision trophy at the winners' press conference, Malmo, May 2024

headline: Apple Intelligence
text: At its developer conference Apple announced Apple Intelligence, artificial intelligence features for the iPhone, iPad and Mac, including the use of OpenAI's ChatGPT to improve Siri. Apple has been criticised for falling behind in AI. The shares rose and briefly made Apple the world's most valuable company again, ahead of Microsoft.
imageCaption: The Steve Jobs Theater at Apple Park, Cupertino, where Apple holds its keynotes

headline: The most valuable company in the world
text: On 18 June Nvidia's market value passed 3.3 trillion dollars, making it the most valuable company in the world, ahead of Microsoft and Apple.
imageCaption: Jensen Huang with EU foreign-policy chief Josep Borrell, May 2024

headline: Nvidia becomes the world's most valuable company
text: On 18 June Nvidia passed Microsoft and Apple as the world's most valuable company, at more than 3.3 trillion dollars. It closed above 2 trillion for the first time only on 1 March.
imageCaption: Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang, California, May 2024

headline: Boeing buys back Spirit and picks Kelly Ortberg
text: On 1 July Boeing agreed to buy Spirit AeroSystems, the Wichita supplier that builds 737 fuselages and was spun off from Boeing in 2005, in an all-stock deal worth about 4.7 billion dollars. On 31 July it named Kelly Ortberg, a former head of Rockwell Collins, as chief executive from 8 August. Dave Calhoun, who announced in March that he would step down after the door-plug accident, leaves on 7 August.
imageCaption: Kelly Ortberg, named Boeing's chief executive in July 2024
imageCredit: Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation

headline: Glencore keeps its coal
text: On 7 August, a month after completing the Elk Valley purchase, Glencore dropped the planned coal spin-off: more than 95% of shareholders who expressed a view wanted to keep coal for its cash flow, which will fund copper growth and payouts. On 5 August it settled the last bribery probes, in Switzerland and the Netherlands, with a CHF2m fine and $150m compensation.
imageCaption: Aerial view of the Mount Owen coal mine complex, New South Wales, Australia

headline: Intel suspends its dividend and cuts 15% of jobs
text: On 1 August Intel reported a second-quarter loss of 1.6 billion dollars, said it will cut more than 15% of its workforce, about 15,000 jobs, and suspend its dividend from the fourth quarter. The shares fell 26% the next day to 21.48 dollars, their worst day in decades.
imageCaption: Intel's headquarters in Santa Clara, California

headline: Tokyo's worst day since 1987 as the yen snaps back
text: The yen hit 161 per dollar in July, its weakest in 37 years, and then the Bank of Japan, which had ended eight years of negative rates in March, raised rates again on 31 July. As traders unwound bets funded with cheap yen, the dollar fell to about 143 yen and on 5 August the Nikkei fell 12.4%, 4,451 points, to 31,458. The next day it gained more than 3,200 points, its biggest daily rise.
imageCaption: The Tokyo Stock Exchange

headline: Berkshire becomes a trillion-dollar company
text: In August Berkshire Hathaway became the first company outside the technology industry in the United States to be valued at more than one trillion dollars. A single Class A share reached 700,000 dollars. Berkshire has substantially increased its holdings of short-term Treasury bills.
imageCaption: Warren Buffett at lunch in Omaha, February 2024

headline: Schneider out, Laurent Freixe in
text: Nestlé announced in August that chief executive Mark Schneider is leaving and that Laurent Freixe, a long-time Nestlé manager, takes over on 1 September. Growth has slowed and the share is well below its high of late 2021.
imageCaption: Ulf Mark Schneider, chief executive of Nestlé

headline: The Fed's first cut in four years, half a point at once
text: On 18 September the Fed cut its rate by half a point to 4.75 to 5 percent, its first cut since 2020, saying it had 'greater confidence that inflation is moving sustainably toward 2 percent'; one member preferred a quarter point. Consumer prices in August were 2.5 percent higher than a year earlier, the lowest since early 2021. Gold averaged 2,571 dollars in September, a record, after central banks bought more than 1,000 tonnes in each of 2022 and 2023.
imageCaption: Fed chairman Jerome Powell at a press conference

headline: 33,000 machinists strike
text: On 13 September more than 33,000 Boeing machinists, mostly around Seattle, went on strike after 94.6% rejected a contract with a 25% raise over four years. Production of the 737, 767 and 777 has stopped.
imageCaption: 777X fuselages inside Boeing's Everett factory

headline: Brake recall and China force a profit warning
text: On 10 September BMW recalled more than 1.5 million cars because of a faulty brake component from the supplier Continental and stopped deliveries of 320,000 cars not yet handed over. Together with weak demand in China, the recall made BMW cut its profit forecast for 2024, and the shares plunged.
source: DW, 'BMW recalls 1.5 million cars over brake issue', 10 September 2024, https://www.dw.com/en/bmw-recalls-15-million-cars-over-brake-issue/a-70182052 (read 2026-10-03); Reuters, 'BMW cuts 2024 outlook on Continental brake issues, shares plunge', 10 September 2024 (headline via Google News) (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: The BMW headquarters tower, Munich

headline: China's slump forces a profit warning
text: On 19 September Mercedes-Benz cut its margin forecast for cars because sales in China, its largest market, are weakening fast. The shares slumped. Other European car makers also issued warnings this month.
source: Reuters, 'Mercedes-Benz cuts margin outlook on weak Chinese market, shares fall', 20 September 2024; Bloomberg, 'Mercedes Slumps After Warning China Rout Is Hurting Profits', 19 September 2024 (headlines via Google News) (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Ola Källenius, chairman of Mercedes-Benz, at talks in China, 2024

headline: Boeing raises 21 billion dollars of new capital
text: On 28 October Boeing sold 112.5 million new shares at 143 dollars and 5 billion dollars of mandatory convertible preferred shares, raising about 21 billion dollars to protect its credit rating. The machinists' strike is still on.
imageCaption: Boeing's headquarters in Arlington, Virginia

headline: Trump's victory lifts Musk's Tesla
text: Donald Trump won the US presidential election on 5 November with the open support of Elon Musk. Tesla shares surged as investors bet that Musk's closeness to the new president will help Tesla. Tesla's value is back above 1 trillion dollars.
source: Reuters, 'Tesla stock extends rally as Musk-Trump alliance fuels gains', 11 November 2024 (headline via Google News) (read 2026-10-03); CNBC, 'Tesla shares close at record high, boosted by 69% pop since Trump election victory', 11 December 2024 (headline via Google News) (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla,_Inc. (market value, read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Elon Musk (second from left) with Donald Trump at Mar-a-Lago, Florida, 14 November 2024

headline: Trump wins a second term
text: Donald Trump won the presidential election of 5 November against Vice President Kamala Harris, who replaced Joe Biden as candidate in July, with 312 electoral votes; Republicans also won the Senate. He promises tariffs, tax cuts and mass deportations. Tesla shares jumped on bets that its chief Elon Musk, who gave more than 130 million dollars to help Trump win, will benefit, and Tesla's market value passed one trillion dollars on 8 November.
imageCaption: President Biden walks to the Oval Office with President-elect Donald Trump, Washington, 13 November 2024

headline: Gelsinger is pushed out
text: Intel announced on 2 December that Pat Gelsinger has retired as chief executive and left the board, effective 1 December. Finance chief David Zinsner and Michelle Johnston Holthaus are interim co-chief executives while the board searches for a successor. The shares are down about half this year.
source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/50863/000005086324000173/a12012024form8-kex991.htm (read 2026-10-03, via search summary); https://www.cnbc.com/2024/12/02/intel-ceo-pat-gelsinger-is-out.html (read 2026-10-03, via search summary)
imageCaption: Pat Gelsinger, Intel's chief executive

headline: Assad's rule collapses in Syria
text: Rebels led by Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham, who began an offensive on 27 November, took Aleppo and then Damascus on 8 December. President Bashar al-Assad fled to Russia, ending more than half a century of his family's rule. Iran, which backed him through the civil war, has lost its main ally in the Arab world and its land route to Hezbollah.
imageCaption: Syrians celebrate in Damascus after the fall of Assad's government, 11 December 2024

headline: Walmart buys Vizio after a year of big gains
text: In December Walmart completed its 2.3 billion dollar purchase of the television maker Vizio, to sell more advertising on screens in people's homes. Walmart's shares have risen by about 70% this year, as its online shop, advertising and membership businesses grow.
imageCaption: A Vizio smart-TV remote
